transactions.path: Positive homogeneity in strain increment; derivatives per normalized path fraction, not per second. No elapsed-time creep or hold evolution.
transactions.trial_commit_rollback: Trial starts from committed sigma/e; failed increment restores parent. Adaptive integration and defect estimates are project choices, not Eqs40–46.
transactions.spin: Source uses Jaumann objective stress rate; current supported profile restricts spin to zero. Passive tensor covariance does not establish finite-rotation transport.
transactions.tangent: Norm(de) is nonsmooth at zero; no globally smooth tangent is inferred.

unsupported: complete physical applicability throughout the project numerical domain

initialization_notes.root_defaults: Illustrative Karlsruhe/Fellin-summary constants, not the original TableI or fitted Wichtmann constants. Root sigma=100kPaI,e=.7 are examples only.
initialization_notes.source_ambiguity: Fig13/14 captions place e=.67 at beginning of shearing at -100kPaI; body p264 gives initial .67 then .633 after isotropic preparation to traceT=-300kPa. Fig10 text/legends also differ. Preserve ambiguity; do not invent a preparation deck.

state_semantics_evidence.sigma: Eqs1/40 Cauchy tensor with objective rate; fixed spatial zero-spin restriction. Passive transformation Q sigma Q^T.
state_semantics_evidence.e: Eq2 scalar void ratio; invariant under passive basis changes.

sources.locator: VW96Eqs1–2,40–46 and AppendixC; general eight-parameter host

source_domain_notes: AppendixC characterizes F on u=tanpsi=0 and 0<u<sqrt(2), with C=cos(3theta) in [-1,1]. Root guards admit some algebraic continuations beyond this stated range. This is not itself a demonstrated Eq40 error or a source-mandated runtime guard.
No explicit universal principal-compression rejection rule was found. Mixed-sign principal stress can occur even inside u<sqrt(2). Physical applicability needs an explicit reviewed decision.
Strict root ed<e<ei, positive pressure cutoff, F>0 and fb>0 are the actual executable admission; they do not prove complete physical admissibility.
